item.title: European Unrest Prompts Military Deployments; West Bank Violence Escalates: On Air, October 22, 2026
item.description:
French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu announced new curfews would be imposed where necessary, with local authorities coordinating decisions. Targeted curfews helped maintain calm overnight into Tuesday, following days of widespread unrest. Police confirmed Monday night passed without major incidents across France, though more than 2,000 people were arrested during the weekend.
Israeli settlers burned a welcome sign at the entrance of Burqa, a village east of Ramallah in the occupied West Bank, on Tuesday. Sayel Kanaan, head of the Burqa council, stated settlers ignited vehicle tires on the sign's stonework. Israeli police detained 10 people in connection with West Bank settler attacks, which included an assault on US photojournalist Heidi Levine and European diplomats.
France will deploy military forces, specifically the Sentinelle force, during upcoming protests planned for Saturday, October 24. Interior Minister Laurent Nunez announced the deployment aims to free police and gendarmes for maintaining order. Prime Minister Lecornu stated police deployment for Saturday's demonstrations would be massive, seeking an immediate return to order.
French security forces arrested a man believed linked to ultra-left movements over the burning down of the Limoges town hall. Anti-terror police investigate the suspected arson of the 1883 building, whose roof and belfry collapsed on Saturday, October 17. The man was arrested by officers from the specialized RAID police unit in Val d’Issoire.
Italy's government deploys 500 army troops to Milan to bolster security following a weekend of riots, looting, and clashes. Deputy Prime Minister Matteo Salvini announced the troop deployment, stating it moved "from words to action." The unrest occurred during demonstrations against the rising cost of living and poor public services, leading to smashed windows and looted shops.
Sudan's Foreign Ministry summoned Ambassador Essam Mohamed Karrar to express strong objection to a drone strike in the Abyei region. Abyei's information minister, Yohana Akol Ngor, stated the Amiet Market was hit by several drones, including a fuel depot used by Sudan's paramilitary Rapid Support Forces. The UN spokesperson Stéphane Dujarric expressed alarm over continued deadly drone strikes across Sudan.
The US Homeland Security Department ordered civilian federal agencies to remove and stop acquiring products and services using China's DeepSeek AI model. The US government cited "multiple threat vectors" and concerns about sensitive data transfer to China due to DeepSeek's servers. China’s commerce ministry condemned the US order, calling for an immediate reversal of the restrictive measures.
The Department of Justice charged 28 individuals, including green card holders, with crimes related to voter fraud in California. Eleven of the accused were arrested as part of "Operation Protect the Vote." The DOJ stated all 28 are lawful permanent residents not permitted to vote, facing charges of unlawful voting and falsely claiming U.S. citizenship.
Christiane Amanpour, CNN's chief international anchor, will leave the network in June 2027 after 43 years. She announced her daily show "Amanpour" on CNN International will scale back to once a week in early 2027 and conclude in May. Amanpour, 68, plans to continue her podcast "The Ex Files" with her ex-husband, Jamie Rubin.
President Donald Trump renewed his call for New Mexico to change its name to "New America," stating on Truth Social, "We are not Mexico, we are the United States of America!" He claimed the name change would add great value and prestige to the State and boost residents' pride.
Full bias analysis and source spectrum: https://news.voidvision.org/onair/.
